data.title: Robinhood Stock Tokens to Add Physical Redemption and Voting Features, Vlad Tenev Says
data.description: Robinhood co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev said the company’s stock tokens will soon support physical redemption and voting features. According to Odaily, Tenev made the remarks in a recent statement.

data.title: UBS Adds Senior Hires to US Investment Bank Industrial Team
data.description: UBS Group AG has hired a series of senior bankers for its investment bank to strengthen industrial coverage in North America, according to a memo seen by Bloomberg.

data.title: ECB's Cipollone Says €200 Note Still Has Role Despite Laundering Risks
data.description:
European Central Bank Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said concerns about money laundering should not stop issuance of a €200 bill, according to Bloomberg.

He said there are now better ways to clean up illicit earnings than using banknotes.

data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump Says He Plans $5,000 “Trump Dividend” for All Adults
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. is reaping trillions of dollars in economic gains, investment, and major success, and plans to distribute a $5,000 "Trump dividend" to all adults nationwide, a proposal criticized by Democrats who want it blocked but Trump said it will be implemented.

data.title: Trader Unipcs Says He Will Not Sell EMBER Holdings Despite Short-Term Volatility
data.description:
Trader Unipcs said his investment thesis for EMBER remains unchanged and that he will not sell his position because of short-term volatility. According to Odaily, his EMBER holdings are worth about $687,500, with unrealized gains of about $271,700.

Unipcs previously said EMBER has shown strong resilience near its all-time high even as the broader market remains weak. He also said he would not be surprised if the token continued to rise sharply after returning to its all-time high, and added that some negative discussion around the Bubblemaps cluster and its partnership with Meteora has been overstated by the market.

data.title: Fed Overnight Reverse Repo Usage Falls to $1.42 Billion
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Federal Reserve overnight reverse repurchase agreement usage was $1.42 billion on Monday, with four counterparties, down from $5.255 billion in the previous trading day.

data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Apple launched Siri AI and began rolling out an English beta version today, with expansion to five languages planned; the feature will not initially be available on iOS, iPadOS, or watchOS in the European Union.

data.title: Oil Tanker Rates Top $1 Million a Day as Strait of Hormuz Risk Cuts Supply
data.description:
The cost of hiring an oil tanker on the industry’s benchmark route rose above $1 million a day for the first time, according to Bloomberg.

The surge came as the Iran war left too few ships willing to cross the Strait of Hormuz to pick up cargoes.

data.title: STOCKS | AI Rout Raises Diversification Case After 13-to-1 Fund-Flow Gap
data.description:
AI-focused investors have poured billions of dollars into technology stocks for months while largely overlooking the rest of the market, according to Bloomberg.

Monday’s selloff in the sector came after industry leaders called for a slower pace of technology development, a reminder of the case for diversification.

data.title: Fed Rate Hike Could Lift Borrowing Costs as Inflation Hits 3.4% in August
data.description:
According to CNBC, market-watchers expect the Federal Reserve to raise the target federal funds rate by one-quarter of a percentage point on Wednesday as energy prices rise and tensions with Iran persist. The consumer price index climbed again last month, putting annual inflation at 3.4% in August, with higher oil and gas prices a major driver, government data showed. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has said he is committed to bringing inflation back to the central bank's 2% target, and a rate increase would be the Fed's first in more than three years.

The report said higher rates would likely push up borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, including mortgages, car loans and credit card debt, while savers could earn more on deposits. Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's, said credit card rates, which are already above 20%, would rise to record highs once the Fed moves. WalletHub said the average APR on a 48-month new car loan is expected to rise by about 12 basis points in the months after a 25-basis-point Fed hike.

The article said the 10-year Treasury yield topped 4.95% last week, its highest level since October 2023, and the average rate on the 30-year fixed mortgage moved above 7% for the first time in more than a year. LoanDepot chief investment officer and head economist Jeff DerGurahian said a Fed hike would not automatically lift 30-year mortgage rates if markets had already priced it in and investors viewed the move as a measured step toward 2% inflation. Adjustable-rate mortgages and home equity lines of credit are tied more directly to the prime rate, while federal student loan rates are fixed and private student loan rates can move with benchmarks such as Libor, prime or Treasury bill rates.

data.title: STOCKS | LPL Says U.S. Economy Resembles Late 1990s as AI Investment Supports Spending
data.description:
Investopedia reported on September 15 that U.S. stocks have often struggled in the first months after the Federal Reserve begins raising rates. According to PANews, LPL Financial Chief Equity Strategist Jeff Buchbinder reviewed six Fed tightening cycles since 1994 and found that the S&P 500 typically weakened shortly after the first rate hike, while performance one year later was much stronger than in the initial months.

LPL said the average return was lifted by an especially strong move after the March 1997 rate hike, when the S&P 500 rose 42% over the following year. The firm said the current macro backdrop is different from 2022 and is closer to the late 1990s, with the economy still growing and a new cycle of technology investment forming.

LPL Financial said the current AI investment boom may support corporate capital spending and the technology sector for a period of time, partly offsetting the pressure that higher rates place on stock valuations.

data.title: AI Era Linked to Weaker Pay and Jobs for College Graduates
data.description:
A new study found that the rise of artificial intelligence has coincided with a significant decline in initial earnings and employment among graduates in the most exposed college majors, according to Bloomberg.

The report said the trend could affect career outcomes for years afterward.

data.title: Puig to Buy Remaining Isdin Stake for €1.2 Billion
data.description: Puig Brands SA agreed to buy the remaining 50% of skincare brand Isdin it did not already own for €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion), according to Bloomberg. The deal gives Puig full control of Isdin.

data.title: U.S. Refiners Rally As Crack Spreads Hit Near-Record Levels
data.description:
According to CNBC, independent oil refiners are benefiting from unusually wide crack spreads as U.S. diesel prices hit $6 per gallon for the first time and Brent crude rose 8.7% last week amid escalating Middle East tensions. Distillate inventories are about 14% below their five-year average, Saudi Arabia shut a key East-West crude pipeline to the Red Sea after damage in an Iraqi attack, and refining margins have risen about 60% quarter to date from the second quarter.

The article said global refining capacity has expanded on paper by 400,000 to 700,000 barrels per day over the past two years, but actual fuel production has fallen about 5%, or roughly 4.2 million barrels per day. It added that Western refiners are running at 98% to 103.5% of capacity, while rebuilding disrupted units and logistics could take 12 to 18 months.

Valero Energy shares are up more than 140% year to date and hit an intraday record of $399.40 on Monday before trading down nearly 2%. Marathon Petroleum has gained nearly 145% this year and reached an all-time intraday high of $409.50 on Monday before slipping less than 1% in midday trading. Phillips 66 has doubled year to date, touched a record $265.43 on Friday, and was down about 1% on Monday after its board approved a $10 billion increase to its buyback program in July.

data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump Says U.S. High-End Weapons Production Is at a Record High
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. President Donald Trump said he had just received a report showing that the number of high-end weapons currently produced by the United States has reached a record high, with related equipment delivered daily to U.S. troops deployed in the Middle East and other regions. He said U.S. defense factories are operating around the clock, with each factory averaging four to five new large buildings under construction, and that the production focus includes Patriot missiles, THAAD missile defense systems, Tomahawk missiles and other Standard missile systems, while the United States currently holds large inventories of such equipment.
